target: Smooth 60 fps on live vlang.io; still open
scope: Changed native layer contents after updateLayer, with changed scroll position; entire first-to-last input period. Not physical display scanout.

protocol.title: V — The V Programming Language
protocol.profile_cache: Fresh empty private profile/cache; direct HTTPS; automatic author scripts; OS filesystem/shader caches retained.

policies.visible_copy: Off: high-threshold pairs both regress; lower-threshold pairs remain mixed after confirming 107 reduced input-window copies and 247,077,552 omitted bytes.
policies.empty_pointwise: Off: prototype has mixed means and slightly worse p95. Later final-code pairs regress; an owned focused native job overlaps the second candidate, excluding optimization acceptance.
policies.software_pointwise: Off: exact same-input comparison succeeds for 106 input-window filter outputs, but both mean/p95 pairs regress: 88.83 to 85.13 and 87.65 to 79.93 publications/s. No performance credit.

limitations: Native publications do not establish physical display scanout. Mean throughput above 60 does not establish smooth 60 fps.
All complete pairs and failed attempts are retained. Host load and input cadence are recorded per run; variation and contention limit causal attribution.

The first empty-pointwise cohort uses the prototype bitmap scan compiled from dirty source at head 3eac0d2ac. The final cohort uses the committed early-return scan in the newer f3619474e bundle. Do not treat prototype timing as final-code verification.
An owned focused native verification job overlaps the final empty-filter second candidate. That cohort supplies no optimization acceptance; the first pair also regresses mean and p95.

The first empty-filter fixture expected a one-level-alpha fractional edge to remain nonzero after Quartz coverage. The final guard case uses an opaque edge; separate direct and frame cases retain one-level-alpha coverage checks.

Doubling the compact-filter corpus initially exceeded the unchanged 3 GiB runtime guard. Per-case autorelease pools now release comparison buffers; final optimized and sanitized runs complete well below that budget.

Two shared production builds fail on unrelated in-progress CSS mutable-scalar arguments. The other session corrects its source; no foreign source is edited here. Later successful receipts and all failures are retained.
Same-input software/GPU verification is diagnostic and adds a GPU render. It is excluded from all unprofiled timing arms.
Experimental copy and filter flags remain disabled unless a later recorded decision explicitly enables them.
